title: Mauryan Art and Architecture

cards.b: Mauryan art is the first large body of stone art in India. Prelims asks about pillars, stupas, caves, polish and the Didarganj Yakshi. It also shows two streams: court art and popular art.

Court art: Ashokan pillars, palace at Kumrahar (Pataliputra, with an 80-pillar hall, Persepolis-like). Popular art: Yaksha and Yakshi figures, terracotta, caves. Wood was used earlier; Ashoka moved to stone. Foreign influence (Persian, Greek) is debated.

Monolithic, of Chunar sandstone, 12 to 15 m tall, with a smooth Mauryan polish and an animal capital on a bell-shaped lotus base and abacus. Examples: Lauriya Nandangarh, Sanchi, Rampurva (bull, lion), Sankisa (elephant), Allahabad (Kosambi), Sarnath. The Sarnath lion capital has four lions and four wheels on the abacus; India’s state emblem, adopted 26 January 1950, comes from it.

Ashoka is credited with 84,000 stupas. Sanchi’s Great Stupa (Madhya Pradesh) began under Ashoka as a brick stupa; the stone casing and toranas came later (Shunga, Satavahana). Bharhut and Sanchi stupas show Buddha as symbols: wheel, footprints, bodhi tree. A stupa has anda, harmika, chhatra, medhi and vedika.

The Barabar and Nagarjuni hills (Bihar) caves were donated to Ajivikas by Ashoka and his grandson Dasharatha. Lomas Rishi cave has a carved elephant frieze. The walls have a mirror polish. Caves imitate wooden huts. They begin the tradition of rock-cut architecture later seen at Karle and Ajanta.

The Didarganj Yakshi (Patna museum) stands about 1.6 m, polished sandstone, a Mauryan masterpiece. Parkham Yaksha (Mathura), Besnagar Yakshi, Dhauli elephant (Odisha, the first Buddhist rock sculpture). The Rampurva bull shows Persian-like detail.

Marshall and Mortimer Wheeler saw Persian influence (bell capital, polish, Kumrahar hall). Others say the idea of a pillar is Vedic, and the carving tradition was local. Inscriptions in Kharosthi and Aramaic show contact. A balanced view calls it a blend.

The Sarnath capital is national emblem (the bull and horse on the base, “Satyameva Jayate” in Devanagari). The 24-spoke Ashoka Chakra is on the national flag. The 2022 new Parliament’s emblem was a controversy about its lion style. Sarnath Museum holds the original.
